The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Another Trump memecoin dinner advertised for token's top investors. The company managing the memecoin calls the November event the "most exclusive dinner in the world." Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto for Advisors: The CLARITY Act failed, but the rules came anyway. The report adds another detail to the day's market picture. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

NEAR Intents hit by $3.8 million exploit as crypto's rough year of hacks continues. The popular cross-chain trading system said it will reimburse losses after a bug affected deposits and withdrawals across several networks. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin posts tentative gains as rates drop ahead of Friday's jobs report. The euro is losing ground versus the greenback as spiking French bond yields revive memories of the European sovereign debt crisis. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Illinois agrees to six-month delay of crypto tax as industry continues court battle. Both sides agreed the 0.2% tax should be put off until July 1, if the court approves the deal, which will let the state and industry focus on the legal dispute. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto lost $1.26 billion in hacks while bitcoin bulls enjoyed a monster quarter. Your day-ahead look for Oct. 1, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $84,746 with a +0.98% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,698.6 with a +0.76% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto ETFs End 8-Week Outflow Streak With $282M Inflows as Bitcoin and Ethereum Demand Rebounds
items.description:
After two months of relentless selling pressure, cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have finally posted their first week of positive flows, signaling a potential improvement in institutional sentiment toward digital assets.

Global crypto investment products attracted $281.8 million in net inflows last week, ending an eight-week stretch of outflows that erased more than $7 billion from the sector. [...] Daily flows reflected continued uncertainty among investors. Funds attracted more than $265 million on July 6, the strongest single-day inflow since early May, before sharply slowing the following day.

The middle of the week saw renewed outflows before demand recovered again on Friday with another positive session.

Despite the improvement, the latest inflows remain small compared with the more than $8 billion that exited Bitcoin ETFs over the previous eight weeks. [...] US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $197.4 million in net inflows during the week ending July 10, breaking an eight-week streak of outflows that had persisted since the second week of May.

The weekly figure was driven primarily by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which continued to dominate the market.

IBIT attracted nearly $292 million during the week, offsetting significant withdrawals from Grayscale's GBTC, Fidelity's FBTC, and ARK 21Shares' Bitcoin ETF.

items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’s Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On April 1, 2026, the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the GENIUS Act), a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

# Bitcoin At $84K: How Macro And Geopolitics Shape The Next Move

Bitcoin is pinned near $83K–$84K as surging bond yields and Middle East tensions cap upside, despite ongoing corporate treasury accumulation.

Tuesday, September 29, 2026at12:01 PM

•6 min read [...] ## Conclusion

Bitcoin’s current consolidation near $83,000–$84,000 is a textbook example of how macro and geopolitical forces can cap upside even when structural demand, such as corporate treasury buying, remains in place. Higher long-term yields, bond market volatility, and Middle East tensions are dampening risk appetite, leaving BTC trapped below a key resistance zone and forcing traders to adapt. [...] The important nuance is that long-term data show Bitcoin and Treasury yields do not have a stable, reliable correlation. Sometimes Bitcoin rallies alongside higher yields; at other times, both fall together. The current episode is less about yields themselves and more about bond market volatility and uncertainty over central bank policy. Elevated rate volatility makes investors more cautious, and that caution spills over into crypto.

The cryptocurrency market has entered a powerful rebound phase, led by Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), as sentiment shifts sharply from defensive to risk-on.

The rally accelerated on 19 August 2026 following two major developments.

First, President Trump hosted leading cryptocurrency industry representatives at the White House and urged Congress to advance the CLARITY Act, strengthening expectations of a more supportive U.S. regulatory environment for digital assets. [...] However, the market is now transitioning from the initial rally phase into a much more important confirmation phase.

## Bottom Line

The immediate outlook for Bitcoin and Ethereum has turned decisively more bullish, but the market has now entered a critical confirmation stage.

The bullish case would strengthen if: [...] The White House's renewed support for clearer crypto regulation has strengthened expectations surrounding the future U.S. digital-asset framework.

At the same time, larger Treasury buybacks helped ease pressure in the bond market and improve broader risk sentiment.

These catalysts were then amplified by a powerful short squeeze, pushing Bitcoin above $70,000 and Ethereum above $2,200.

items.description:
Article cover image

# Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

Coin Gabbar

Coin Gabbar@coin\_gabbar\_·

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
